text:
Maya R.: Heads-up: publishing Community Ops Patterns Kit v0.1.0 — a compact repo with reusable incident/runbook scaffolds, CI job templates, ownership playbooks, and a lightweight local dev CLI. :rocket:
Maya R.: Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-ops-patterns (tag: v0.1.0)
Maya R.: Quick install for the local helper:```bash
npm i -g @redwood/ops-kit@0.1.0
ops-kit init # scaffold a runbook in ./runbooks/my-service
```
tooling-bot: release published: community-ops-patterns@0.1.0 — assets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-ops-patterns/releases/tag/v0.1.0 — changelog: "initial scaffolds, CI templates, ownership docs"
Luis: Love the CI job templates. Are the GitHub Actions reusable across enterprise forks?
Maya R.: Yes — actions are split into infra/actions and are MIT. We included examples for self-hosted runners and for GitHub-hosted. See docs/enterprise-usage.md for recommended secrets/KMS patterns.
Fiona: Nice. Is there any change to our community governance (e.g., who can merge release PRs)?
Maya R.: Not changing company policy. The repo includes a MAINTAINERS.md that suggests a 2-person approval rule for community PRs and a release checklist that requires one official committer sign-off. For external maintainers we recommend CODEOWNERS and a release tag review.
Luis: Any specific onboarding for new maintainers?
tooling-bot: Onboarding checklist created: /docs/maintainer-quickstart.md — includes local env boot, test commands, and a "first-PR" guide.
Maya R.: We added a short governance appendix: how to request maintainer rights, a rotation cadence (6 months suggested), and a lightweight conflict resolution flow.
Fiona: Can we run a short demo at the community meetup next week? I can demo scaffolding + the CI smoke tests if we have a recorder.
Maya R.: Absolutely — scheduling a 30-min demo slot Thursday 4pm PT, will record and post a short how-to video. Signup here: https://cal.com/redwood/community-ops-demo
Luis: Are there any breaking changes expected for the runbook-lint rules or naming conventions? I maintain a small org that might adopt these templates.
Maya R.: v0.1.0 is intentionally stable and conservative. We documented the runbook-lint rules under docs/linting.md and included an opt-in config file to keep backwards compatibility. Major breaking changes will be communicated in a CHANGELOG and a deprecation schedule.
tooling-bot: Note: repo contains a CONTRIBUTING.md with optional CLA and DCO instructions. If your org requires CLA enforcement, enable the bot and add the label `cla-required`.
infra-bot: Heads up: if you enable the infra templates in a repo, add the label `infra-impact` when opening the PR so SRE gets automated review.
Fiona: I'll take the demo slides and a short FAQ. Can someone drop a link to the deploy smoke test command?
Maya R.: Command is in docs/smoke-tests.md: `./scripts/smoke-run --target=staging --short` — it's included in the CI job example.
Luis: Thanks! I'll open an issue to request an additional template for GDPR incident playbooks.
Maya R.: Please do — tagged as `enhancement`. We're happy to accept PRs. Big thanks to the folks who contributed: @Fiona @Luis and the early testers. We'll iterate fast based on feedback. :clap:
